content: While taking this medication, it is essential to monitor your health through regular medical and laboratory tests, such as viral load, T-cell counts, liver function, cholesterol, triglyceride levels, and blood sugar levels. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if more than four hours have passed since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The suspension can be stored at room temperature or in the refrigerator, as refrigeration may improve its taste. Do not freeze the suspension. Avoid storing this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. Fosamprenavir belongs to a class of drugs called protease inhibitors. It may be administered with ritonavir, another protease inhibitor, to enhance (boost) the levels of fosamprenavir in your body. However, fosamprenavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items (e.g., needles, syringes, toothbrushes, razors) that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Before starting this medication, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. If you are taking the suspension form of fosamprenavir, shake the bottle well before each dose. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. Do not use a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. Adults should take the suspension without food, while children should take it with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, other medications you may be taking, and whether you have previously used protease inhibitors to treat HIV. For children, the dosage is also based on age and weight. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, nonprescription drugs, and herbal products. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, take more or less than prescribed, or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s guidance, even for a short time. Common side effects of this medication include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Fosamprenavir may commonly cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking fosamprenavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, amprenavir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as propylene glycol in the suspension) that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Fosamprenavir may increase cholesterol and triglyceride levels in your blood, which could raise your risk of heart problems, such as a heart attack. HIV infection itself can also contribute to this effect. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as ways to lower your risk of heart disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and fosamprenavir may be part of that treatment. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of fosamprenavir from your body, which may impact how it works. Examples include apalutamide, etravirine, and rifampin. Fosamprenavir can also affect the removal of other medications from your body, potentially altering their effectiveness. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patch, or ring), which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Regular laboratory and medical tests (e.g., viral load, T-cell counts, liver function, cholesterol/triglyceride levels, blood sugar levels) should be conducted while taking this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments.
